title: India Hospital Receivables, TPA Deductions & CGHS DSO Report
h1: The 2026–2027 Indian Hospital Receivables & TPA/CGHS Delay Index: DSO Benchmarks Across Private Healthcare
metaTitle: India Hospital Receivables, TPA Deductions & CGHS DSO Report
metaDescription: Benchmark analysis of Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) across Cashless TPAs, CGHS/ECHS/PM-JAY, Corporate Credit & Post-Discharge Patient Undertakings in India.

payerSegments.statutoryTargetDays: 30 Days (IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance)
payerSegments.primaryDisputeTypes: Arbitrary consumable cuts, room-rent proportional deduction, pharmacy markup disallowance, package unbundling disputes
payerSegments.statutoryRemedy: IRDAI Health Insurance Master Circular (Bank Rate + 2% Penal Interest) + Commercial Courts Act 2015 s.2(1)(c)(xx)
payerSegments.recoveryEfficiency: High via Advocate Statutory Notice & IRDAI Bima Bharosa escalation

payerSegments.primaryDisputeTypes: UTIITSL portal query loops, budgetary allocation freezes, procedural rejection of implant invoices, retrospective audit cuts
payerSegments.statutoryRemedy: Section 80 CPC 60-Day Mandatory Notice to Ministry + High Court Art. 226 Writ of Mandamus (ABL International doctrine)
payerSegments.recoveryEfficiency: Very High once Section 80 CPC notice & Writ jurisdiction are invoked

payerSegments.payerCategory: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY & State Health Schemes
payerSegments.primaryDisputeTypes: Transaction Management System (TMS) pre-auth rejections, State Health Agency (SHA) treasury release delays, biometric mismatch cuts
payerSegments.statutoryRemedy: District & State Grievance Redressal Committee (DGRC/SGRC) + High Court Mandamus for admitted scheme claims
payerSegments.recoveryEfficiency: Moderate-to-High with structured SLA claim documentation

payerSegments.payerCategory: Corporate Credit & PSU Medical Desks (BHEL, NTPC, ONGC, Corporates)
payerSegments.primaryDisputeTypes: Unreconciled credit letters, employee separation without medical clearance, attendant cost disallowance, billing code mismatch
payerSegments.statutoryRemedy: Order XXXVII CPC Summary Suit on Credit Letters + MSMED Act s.15–18 (for registered healthcare units) + s.43B(h) Income Tax Act
payerSegments.recoveryEfficiency: Extremely High; corporate debtors cure rapidly upon legal notice

payerSegments.primaryDisputeTypes: Unreachable attendant phone numbers, disputed billing itemization, cancelled credit cards, stopped-payment discharge cheques
payerSegments.statutoryRemedy: Indian Contract Act s.126 (Attendant Co-Guarantee) + NI Act s.4 (Promissory Note) + s.138 (Cheque Dishonour) + Order XXXVII CPC
payerSegments.recoveryEfficiency: 72% Cure Rate when backed by stamped Promissory Note & 15-day Advocate Notice

benchmarksByBedCapacity.category: Small Nursing Homes & Daycare Clinics (10–49 Beds)
benchmarksByBedCapacity.primaryBottleneck: Lack of dedicated in-house legal/RCM desk; vulnerable to TPA unilateral deductions and CGHS bureaucratic exhaustion
High reliance on empanelled schemes (CGHS/ECHS/PM-JAY) creating 6–12 month cash-flow crunches on doctor fee disbursements

benchmarksByBedCapacity.category: Large Multi-Specialty & Corporate Tertiary Hubs (200+ Beds)
benchmarksByBedCapacity.primaryBottleneck: Aggressive TPA short-settlements, package unbundling clawbacks, and complex corporate credit reconciliation delays

methodology.sampleFrame: Aggregated operational recovery dossiers, anonymized hospital accounts receivable ledgers, public filings of listed Indian healthcare networks (Apollo, Fortis, Max, Narayana, Aster, Medanta), trade representations by the Association of Healthcare Providers India (AHPI) and Indian Medical Association (IMA), and IRDAI/CAG statutory audits for FY 2025–2027.
inclusionCriteria: Private multi-specialty hospitals, single-specialty surgical centers, nursing homes, and diagnostic chains operating in India
Cashless claims submitted to IRDAI-licensed Third-Party Administrators (TPAs) and standalone health insurance companies
Empanelled government scheme billings (CGHS, ECHS, PM-JAY, ESIC) processed through UTIITSL or National Health Authority TMS
Documented post-discharge patient balances backed by admission agreements or attendant undertakings
exclusionCriteria: Public government hospitals funded directly via state exchequer budgets
Unverified anonymous social media consumer complaints or non-institutional debt collections
Pre-2023 legacy claims where the 3-year statutory limitation under the Limitation Act 1963 has expired without acknowledgment

definitions.dso: Days Sales Outstanding: (Total Receivables at Period End / Total Credit Healthcare Revenue) * 365 days, measuring the average days required to collect payment after patient discharge or claim generation.
definitions.tpaShortSettlementRate: The percentage variance between the final admissible hospital invoice (adhering to agreed package tariffs) and the net amount disbursed by the TPA/insurer.
definitions.statutoryPenalInterest: Mandatory interest payable by health insurers under the IRDAI Master Circular at RBI Bank Rate + 2% per annum for delays beyond 30 days from document completion.
definitions.dischargeUndertaking: A legally compliant contract executed under Section 126 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and Section 4 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 by the patient attendant securing payment without detaining the patient.

methodology.dataIntegrity: Data is published to provide empirical transparency for healthcare CFOs, medical trade bodies, and institutional investors. Statutory provisions, IRDAI master circular citations, and judicial precedents reflect confirmed legal doctrines across Indian High Courts and the Supreme Court of India.
